verdict.analysis:
Response A attempted the task but did not complete it. The run ended abnormally ('turn_cap (did not finish normally)'), leaving the proofs/ folder in a messy state with multiple backup and temporary files. The final summary claims work is done but acknowledges "Remaining: The studio_shot.jpg and removal of the XMP sidecar need final processing," indicating incomplete execution. The user explicitly stated they want files overwritten in place with no renamed or duplicate copies.

Response B successfully completed the task. All files were cleaned of AI metadata (C2PA, JUMBF, Firefly, Imagen markers removed), rights and copyright information was preserved or added appropriately, ICC profiles were maintained byte-for-byte, and no re-encoding occurred. The delivered proofs/ folder contains only the five cleaned files (label_back.jpg, moodboard.webp, sleeve_front.png, studio_shot.jpg, studio_shot.xmp) plus two documentation files (README.txt, VERIFICATION_REPORT.txt). 

Response B's verification approach was thorough and manual: strings scanning for AI signatures, byte-level pattern matching for known AI markers, JPEG trailer inspection, structural analysis of metadata segments/chunks, and MD5 verification of compressed image data to prove no re-encoding. The detailed reports document exactly what was found and removed in each file.

The visual inspection of delivered images confirms both responses preserved the pixel content correctly (the images look identical to the originals), but only Response B delivered a clean, ready-to-ship folder state without extraneous files.
